Agent assist gains full support playbooks.

FOR AGENTS

Agent assist for support: the support call playbook is rewritten in full (frustration, repeat callers, a callback that never came, a broken promise, billing and debit orders, orders and deliveries, log-ins, long waits, being passed around, wanting it in writing, another language, a bad line and why we verify), with listening first, reading the history, saying what happens next and by when, asking before a hold, warm transfers and closing well. It listens for how callers here say it ("still not sorted", "nobody comes back to me") and for common Afrikaans and isiZulu phrases.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS

More ready-made playbooks: complaints and escalations (a formal complaint, the ombudsman or a regulator, social media, legal threats, a vulnerable customer, an abusive caller), support for retail and online orders, banking and financial services, utilities and municipal services, and medical aid; and for a business technology provider, phone system, contact centre platform, printer, security and CCTV, solar and backup power support, LTE, APN and wireless faults, and growing an account. A playbook now holds 150 objections and 80 next steps.

FOR PLATFORM OPERATORS

Sell rate cards: set what clients pay per call by destination (Platform → Billing → Sell rate cards). Import a rate card file (destination prefix, billing increment, grace and rate per second), change part of it by a percentage as you import (for example +20% on international), and choose the date it takes effect: each import is a new version, and every call is priced by the version in force when it was made. A card is chosen on a plan, and a tenant can have its own card or negotiated prices for some destinations. Statements show South African and international calls apart. Tenants without a card keep their flat price per minute. Resellers have the same page for their own cards.

Carrier rates by carrier and network: each carrier can have its own rate card, by mobile network (Vodacom, MTN, Cell C, Telkom mobile), fixed lines, or prefix, with the default card for the rest; every call now records the carrier that carried it, and is costed by that carrier's rate.

Ported numbers costed right: connect a number lookup (hlr-lookups.com) under Platform → Carrier rates → Number lookups, and each mobile number is looked up once a month and costed by the network it is on now, not the one it was first issued to. Test a number there first. Without a lookup, or when one fails, the number's prefix is used, as before.

Tax rates: the standard rates offered for a new organisation's country were checked against each country's revenue authority and seven corrected (Russia, Kazakhstan, Fiji, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Liberia, Bhutan); Bulgaria's currency is now the euro.

Fixes: a mailbox that stops answering no longer holds up every other mailbox, journey, broadcast and send (it is tried again in five minutes); the platform's own brand shows the Yaxxa mark when no logo is uploaded; billing quantities show two decimals; a guide or link opened in a new tab opens signed in; a dashboard's TV link reads "And 3 more rows." rather than its raw wording; a few desk messages that still showed in English are translated; every help guide has its pictures, retaken."}
